metadata.title: Attention Is All You Need
metadata.tldr: Proposes the Transformer, a sequence transduction architecture based solely on self-attention mechanisms, dispensing entirely with recurrence and convolutions. It achieves state-of-the-art translation quality on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French while requiring significantly less training compute through high parallelizability.

reproducibility.compute_specified: 8x NVIDIA P100 GPUs (12 hours for base model, 3.5 days for big model)

problem.specific_task: Neural Machine Translation (Sequence-to-Sequence Transduction & Constituency Parsing)
problem.problem_statement: How can we design a sequence transduction model that captures long-range dependencies effectively while eliminating the sequential computation bottleneck of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs/LSTMs) and CNNs?
research_questions: Can self-attention alone replace recurrence and convolution in encoder-decoder sequence transduction?
Does constant O(1) sequential path length improve long-range dependency modeling and training throughput?
prior_bottlenecks: Recurrent models (LSTM, GRU) process tokens sequentially (h_t as a function of h_{t-1}), precluding parallelization within training examples.
Convolutional sequence models (ByteNet, ConvS2S) require O(log_k(n)) or O(n/k) layers to connect distant positions, making long-range dependency learning harder.
key_contributions: Introduces the Transformer architecture relying entirely on stacked Multi-Head Self-Attention and point-wise feed-forward layers.
Reduces maximum path length between any two input/output positions to O(1) operations.
Establishes new SOTA BLEU scores on WMT 2014 En-De (28.4) and En-Fr (41.8) at a fraction of prior training cost.

methods.method_summary: An encoder-decoder architecture where the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations to continuous representations using 6 identical layers of Multi-Head Self-Attention and position-wise FFN, and the decoder generates an output sequence auto-regressively using masked self-attention and encoder-decoder cross-attention.

proposed_components.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
proposed_components.role: Computes weighted representation of values V based on compatibility of queries Q and keys K.
proposed_components.mechanism: Computes Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((QK^T) / sqrt(d_k))V. Scaling by 1/sqrt(d_k) prevents large dot products from pushing softmax into regions with vanishingly small gradients.

proposed_components.name: Multi-Head Attention (MHA)
proposed_components.role: Allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
proposed_components.mechanism: Projects Q, K, V h=8 times with learned linear projections to d_k=d_v=64 dimensions, applies Scaled Dot-Product Attention in parallel, concatenates outputs, and projects with W^O.

proposed_components.name: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
proposed_components.role: Injects information about relative and absolute token positions since the model contains no recurrence or convolution.
proposed_components.mechanism: Adds sine and cosine functions of different frequencies PE_{(pos, 2i)} = sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d_model}) to the input embeddings.

proposed_components.name: Warmup Inverse-Square-Root Learning Rate Schedule + Label Smoothing
proposed_components.role: Stabilizes Adam optimizer training and prevents overconfidence during sequence generation.
proposed_components.mechanism: Increases learning rate linearly for warmup_steps=4000, then decays proportionally to step_num^{-0.5}; applies label smoothing epsilon_ls=0.1.

pipeline_steps.description: Tokenize source/target sentences via BPE/word-piece into d_model=512 embeddings and sum with sinusoidal positional encodings.
Pass representations through 6 layers of Multi-Head Self-Attention + Residual/LayerNorm + Position-wise FFN (d_ff=2048).
Apply masked self-attention over previous target tokens, cross-attention over encoder output, and position-wise FFN.
Project decoder output to vocabulary logits via shared weight matrix and decode with beam size=4, length penalty alpha=0.6.

datasets.name: WMT 2014 English-to-German (En-De)
datasets.scale_and_splits: ~4.5 million sentence pairs; encoded with Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) shared 37,000 token vocabulary; tested on newstest2014.
datasets.preprocessing_or_notes: Shared source-target BPE vocabulary of 37k tokens; batched by approximate sequence length (~25,000 source + 25,000 target tokens per batch).

datasets.name: WMT 2014 English-to-French (En-Fr)
datasets.scale_and_splits: 36 million sentence pairs; 32,000 word-piece vocabulary; tested on newstest2014.

datasets.name: Penn Treebank (WSJ Section)
datasets.scale_and_splits: 40K training sentences (WSJ only) and 17M sentences in semi-supervised setting (BerkleyParser corpora).
datasets.preprocessing_or_notes: Used to test whether the Transformer generalizes beyond translation to structural syntactic tasks.

metrics.name: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy)
metrics.purpose: Measures n-gram precision overlap between generated machine translation output and human reference translations.

metrics.name: Training Cost (FLOPs)
metrics.purpose: Estimated total floating-point operations required to train the model (training time × number of GPUs × single-precision FLOP capacity).

metrics.name: Perplexity (PPL)
metrics.purpose: Evaluates token-level language/translation modeling uncertainty on the development set (newstest2013) during ablations.

metrics.name: Section 23 F1 Score (EVALB)
metrics.purpose: Measures precision and recall of labeled syntactic constituents on WSJ Section 23.

experimental_results.best_baseline_name: Petrov et al. (2006) / McClosky et al. (2006)

strengths: Fundamental paradigm shift: demonstrates that self-attention alone outperforms both RNNs and CNNs on sequence transduction.
Dramatic training efficiency gains due to full parallelization across sequence positions during training.
Thorough ablation study (Table 3) isolating the impact of head count h, key dimension d_k, model size, dropout, and sinusoidal vs. learned positional embeddings.
limitations: Quadratic O(n^2 · d) complexity per layer with respect to sequence length n, which becomes a memory/compute bottleneck for very long sequences (images, audio, video).
Autoregressive decoding during inference remains sequential O(n) steps.
future_directions: Restricting self-attention to local neighborhoods of size r around the output position to reduce complexity to O(r · n · d) for long sequences.
Extending the Transformer architecture to multimodal inputs (images, audio, video) and less sequential generation.
